title_clean: The Shorter Series of Questions and Answers — Cūḷavedalla Sutta (MN 44)
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the profound dialogue between Dhammadinnā Therī and Visākha on personality, the Four Noble Truths, and the twenty types of self-view.
description_long:
In this illuminating talk, Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the Cūḷavedalla Sutta (MN 44), featuring one of the rare recorded teachings by a female elder in the early Buddhist texts. Dhammadinnā Therī, ranked foremost among nuns for her gift of preaching, answers her former husband Visākha's penetrating questions about the nature of personality and liberation.

The discussion covers the classical formulation of the Four Noble Truths in terms of 'personality' (sakkāya): how the five aggregates affected by clinging (pañc'upādānakkhandhā) constitute our sense of self, how craving (taṇhā) gives rise to this identity, and the Noble Eightfold Path as the way to cessation. Bhante explores the subtle distinction between clinging and the aggregates themselves, showing how attachment arises through desire and delusion.

Particularly valuable is the detailed analysis of the twenty types of personality-view (sakkāyadiṭṭhi), examining how we relate to each aggregate through four modes: identity, possession, containment, and being contained. This provides practical insight for contemplating our relationship to body, feelings, perceptions, mental formations, and consciousness in meditation and daily life.
